doubts.claim_under_doubt: GET ?tag= gives leadwright's daemon a safe idempotency-search primitive (per list-get.ts's own doc comment and the iterate Goal's framing)
doubts.disproof_attempt: ?tag= is a stateless in-memory read with no server-side check-and-create; unlike the codebase's own existing findByPhaseTaskId()-then-create() pattern (atomic within one request, no await between check and write), a tag-based idempotency check spans two independent daemon-issued HTTP requests (GET then POST) with no lock between them. Two concurrent/racing daemon requests can each see an empty tag search and each POST, creating duplicate tagged tasks.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Either add an atomic server-side dedup-by-tag check mirroring findByPhaseTaskId, or explicitly document that ?tag= is a cheap lookup only -- not an idempotency guarantee -- and that the daemon owns duplicate-prevention itself.
doubts.resolution: The triage assignment's actual scope for Item 1c is narrowly the read-side filter (must NOT build a tag index; only saves the filesystem walk) -- an atomic check-and-create was never asked for and would be a scope expansion. Fixed the list-get.ts comment to explicitly disclaim atomicity and name duplicate-prevention as the daemon's own responsibility, instead of adding server-side dedup logic.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: the ?tag= filter's staleness is bounded by the same acceptable window as the rest of the store's existing reads
doubts.disproof_attempt: SdkSessionsStore.load() runs once at boot; the in-memory map is only refreshed from disk as a side effect of THIS process's own persist(). A GET ?tag= against an idle/different instance can miss a daemon-created row indefinitely, not just within the co-writer note's short merge window.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Disclose the staleness bound explicitly for the idempotency-search use case, or add a re-read-before-answer path for ?tag= specifically if cross-instance freshness is required.
doubts.resolution: This staleness property is pre-existing and identical for every other GET filter (?projectId=, plain list) -- not new architecture, only newly relevant while the comment implied an idempotency guarantee. Finding A's comment fix removes that implication, so no separate disclosure was added for ?tag= specifically -- it applies no differently than to the rest of the unmodified list endpoint.

summary: Attacked all four lenses. Q1 (merge symmetry) and Q2 (create-time vs patch-time race) do NOT hold up any doubt -- mergeRow is field-generic and both create/patch persist() before responding, so no asymmetry exists; Stage 2's confirmation on those two points is correct. Q3 (tag-filter idempotency) surfaced a real, undisclosed gap in the FRAMING (not the implementation): the feature was documented as an idempotency-search primitive but provides no atomicity. Resolved by correcting the comment rather than expanding scope, since atomic dedup was never part of this iterate's assignment.
